findings.title: Login-cache invalidation on update uses the org-aware wrapped model, missing invalidations while the organization is disabled
findings.body: update() fetches the 'original' IDP via getById(), which returns the model wrapped by createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel(). That wrapper overrides isEnabled() to also return false when the linked organization is disabled. registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate() then applies getLoginPredicate() (which includes isEnabled()) to this wrapped model. Consequence: if an organization is disabled and an admin updates one of its IDPs changing hideOnLogin or linkOnly (fields consumers of the login cache do not re-check), both 'original' (isEnabled=false due to disabled org) and 'updated' (hideOnLogin=true) fail the predicate, so no invalidation is registered. The .idp.login caches are not invalidated by organization enable/disable either, so when the organization is re-enabled, the stale cached ID list makes the IDP appear on the login page even though it is now hidden/link-only. The predicate comparison should be done against the unwrapped stored model (raw isEnabled) rather than the organization-aware wrapper.

findings.title: Cleanup in testCacheIDPForLogin registers removal of literal alias "alias" instead of the created IDPs
findings.body: In testCacheIDPForLogin, both cleanup registrations use getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove) with the literal string "alias" instead of the actual alias variable ("idp-alias-" + i / "idp-alias-20"). As a result none of the ~21 identity providers created by the test are removed afterwards, and the deferred remove() calls will hit a non-existent IDP (404) during cleanup, which can fail the test class teardown and pollutes the shared test realm for subsequent tests. The same literal-alias copy/paste already existed in testCacheIDPByOrg and was duplicated here.
